title: Rule compact grammar versioning — lab notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working lab-note describing a compact, versioned rule grammar for control-plane routing. The goal is: a single, small-to-medium JSON rule schema that is easy to lint, fast to parse in control-plane services, and supports safe evolution (additive changes, explicit semantics for breaking changes) and predictable rollouts across multi-region/dedicated/hosted deployments.

Status: in_review — exploratory + test harness in CI. Contains examples, validator output samples, rollout playbook draft, and outstanding questions.

Design goals (brief):
- Compact, human-editable JSON that maps directly to decision engine input (no deep nested optional objects that force special-casing).
- Versioned grammar: rule.version field; validator/agent must support >=1 grammar.
- Backwards compatible by default: additive fields allowed, enums extended only under controlled flags.
- Deterministic resolution: precedence + stable hash-based tie-breakers.
- Signed/origined metadata to allow cryptographic verification in Dedicated/Private (opt-in).

High-level schema (informal):
- id: string (stable rule id)
- version: string (semantic-ish, e.g., "1.0" or "1.1" grammar)
- name: string (human alias)
- precedence: integer (higher wins)
- match: object[] (list of clauses joined with AND by default; OR supported via explicit arrays)
- action: object (route targets + weights + fallbacks)
- rollout: object (strategy, steps, region_overrides)
- meta: object (author, created_at, signature optional)
- constraints: optional checks (max_tokens, allowlist, disallowlist)

Compact example (single rule) - JSON snippet:
{
  "id": "rule.email-routing.v1",
  "version": "1.0",
  "name": "email-workload-model-steer",
  "precedence": 100,
  "match": [
    { "type": "path_prefix", "value": "/v1/generate/email" },
    { "type": "header", "name": "x-workload", "op": "in", "values": ["email", "marketing"] },
    { "type": "region", "op": "in", "values": ["us-east-1"] }
  ],
  "action": {
    "route_to": [
      { "model": "rw-instruct-3b", "variant": "v2-q4", "weight": 80 },
      { "model": "rw-instruct-3b", "variant": "v2", "weight": 20, "fallback": true }
    ],
    "timeout_ms": 1200
  },
  "rollout": {
    "strategy": "progressive",
    "steps": [
      { "percent": 1, "duration_minutes": 60 },
      { "percent": 10, "duration_minutes": 30 },
      { "percent": 50, "duration_minutes": 120 },
      { "percent": 100, "duration_minutes": 0 }
    ],
    "region_overrides": { "eu-west-1": 5, "ap-southeast-1": 2 }
  },
  "meta": { "author": "maya.patel@redwood.ai", "created_at": "2026-02-28T11:10:00Z" }
}

Notes about the snippet: weights within route_to are normalized by the agent. The "fallback" flag marks a target that should be used only if primary targets fail. region_overrides is additive: it seeds initial percent in that region (used when starting rollout); if omitted, global percent applies.

Validation checklist (what our validator enforces):
1) Syntactic: required fields present (id, version, match[], action).
2) Field types: precedence int, rollout.steps is list with numeric percent 0-100, match clause types are from enumerated set.
3) Semantics: weights > 0 unless marked fallback; route_to sum can be <100 (agent scales); fallback targets must have fallback=true.
4) Safety heuristics: rules that match wide path globs (e.g., path_prefix: "/v1/") require additional approval + explicit "wide_match" flag. 
5) Mutually exclusive ops: header op "exists" cannot have values array.
6) Version compatibility: If rule.version > validator_max then reject unless validator runs in "compatibility_mode" and logs a warning.
7) Signing checks: if meta.signature present, verify signature matches author pubkey in keyring (only for Dedicated/Private).
8) Behavioral invariants: precedence must be unique across active rules for the same route_key (we warn, we don't block on transient duplicates during edits).

Validator CLI example (error/warning outputs):
- ERROR [E001] missing required field: action.route_to
- ERROR [E007] rollout.steps[1].percent must be > 0 and <= 100 (found 0)
- WARN  [W014] wide path match '/v1/' without wide_match flag — requires APPROVER tag
- ERROR [E021] rule.version 1.3 uses new enum value "region:continent" not allowed in strict mode
- INFO  [I002] computed stable-hash: 9a7f2d (for audit)

Compatibility & schema evolution rules (proposed):
- Additive fields allowed with default semantics (control-plane applies defaults where missing).
- Removing or renaming a field is breaking: requires major version increment and explicit migration steps in a PR with migration tests.
- Enum extension: allowed only if validator flag "allow_enum_extensions" enabled; otherwise must go through staged rollout and compatibility test harness.
- New match types: permitted in minor version; agents without support treat unknown match type as "no-op" and log. This avoids hard failures in mixed-version fleets — but see security caveat below.

Security caveat: "no-op on unknown match" is convenient but can silently widen matching behavior. For high-sensitivity customers we will require explicit parser upgrades and fail-on-unknown-match in Dedicated mode.

Rollout mechanics (playbook draft):
1) Author rule in branch -> PR -> unit tests + validator passes + migration file (if required).
2) QA: run rule against synthetic traffic for 2 hours in staging (we have a harness that replays 24h production traffic slice). Check: latency P50/P95, error rate, fallback rate, model-quality signal (eval set) 
3) Approvals: if rule.match has wide_match or precedence > 900, require Security + SRE approval.
4) Canary activation: start global progressive rollout with steps per snippet above. Canary region buckets: small subset of users (1% globally, plus region_overrides).
5) Telemetry monitoring: within each step, compute deltas vs baseline for: latency_p50, latency_p99, error_rate, fallback_rate, model_regression(precision@k), cost_per_1k_tokens.
6) Automated gating: if any metric exceeds thresholds (see gating table below) then abort + rollback to previous rule hash.
7) If step passes for duration_minutes, advance to next step.
8) Complete and mark rule as promoted, emit audit event.

Rollout gating thresholds (example):
- latency_p95_increase > 20% => FAIL
- error_rate_absolute_increase > 0.5% => FAIL
- fallback_rate > 1% absolute => WARN & FAIL if sustained 5m
- model_quality_regression (on eval-set) > 1.5% relative => FAIL + require manual review

Automated rollback triggers and behavior:
- Trigger types: statistical signals, infra alerts (node OOM), operator manual abort.
- On trigger: immediately set rollout percent to 0 for new rule in all regions (atomic), route traffic to previous rule hash or default route.
- Emit structured rollback event to timeline + Slack #platform-rollouts and attach diagnostics blob (recent 10m trace and last 1k requests sampled).
- Postmortem: owner must open a short postmortem doc linked to rule id within 48h.

Testing harness (CI):
- Unit tests: verify validator accepts example positive configs and rejects negative ones.
- Integration: small service using the live engine and a mocked model backend to assert routing choices for synthetic headers/paths.
- Property tests: fuzz match clause combinations and assert determinism & no panic.
- Smoke replay: replay 1h production traffic in ephemeral cluster with rule applied and collect metrics.
- Signed-release test: for Dedicated, test that signed rules with tampered payload fail verification.

Operational extras (notes):
- Stable-hash: compute canonical JSON (sorted keys, normalized whitespace) then sha256; publish hash as part of audit trail. This helps rollback and history.
- TTL for rules: optional expiration timestamp — rules beyond expiry are disabled automatically. Useful for short-lived experiments.
- Preview mode: console should let UI users preview match evaluation for a given sample request (headers, path, region) and show why a rule matched/failed.
- Lint rules: prefer explicit ops (==, in, exists) instead of regex by default. Regex allowed but requires extra approval.

Examples of validator output for breaking-change detection (CI):
- FAIL: rule id collision: rule.email-routing.v1 already active with different precedence -> block promotion
- WARN: new enum used: 'geo:continent' (requires feature flag) -> require feature flag toggle in release

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a machine-readable approvals field (approvers: [team:sre, user:alice]) to allow automated gating? (pro: integrates approvals into CI; con: risks bypassing human in last-minute fast-paths). TODO discuss with product ops.
- How strict should unknown-match handling be for Hosted customers? Currently plan: lenient by default, strict for Dedicated. Need legal/security review.
- Should we permit flow-level rate caps inside rule.action (e.g., max_rps_per_user)? Helpful for bursty endpoints but complicates agent runtime.
- Define canonical serializer library (Go + Rust + Python) and publishing cadence. Start with Go v1 then add Rust optimized parser for control-plane hot path.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Diego: prototype validator change to emit stable-hash and test enforcement (ENG-2147).
- Priya: add 10 synthetic replay tests that cover multi-region overrides and fallback scenarios.
- Jonah: draft console preview UI spec and a small CLI preview helper.
- Maya (me): write rollout gating integration with metrics pipeline and document default threshold values in Confluence.

Notes-to-self: Keep grammar surface small. If we need complex behaviors (circuit-breakers, rate-limits) consider referencing external policy objects (policyRef) instead of expanding the rule schema. This keeps core rule compact and fast to parse in runtime.

References and quick links: PR for validator prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/912; Jira ENG-2147 (validator stable-hash); internal replay tool docs: confluence link above.

End of lab notes.

-- maya
